item.title: India Voter-List Purge Draws Growing Backlash
item.description: About 130 million people have been deleted from final or preliminary voter rolls in a process that some government critics have described as opaque.

item.title: Ebola Patient Boarded Commercial Flight, Died Shortly After Arrival
item.description: The man’s death is Kenya’s first reported fatality from Ebola’s Bundibugyo strain, which has killed more than 4,000 people in eastern Congo.

item.title: Former German Spy Chief Arrested on Suspicion of Espionage
item.description: The arrest is one of the biggest scandals to engulf the BND spy agency since its creation in the mid-1950s.

item.title: Brent Futures Fall More than 2% as Middle East Exports Recover, Shipping Risks Persist
item.description: Prices fell Tuesday as traders assessed recovering crude exports against fresh shipping incidents around Hormuz and increased tensions around the Red Sea.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for October 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: These are the accounts that offer the best interest rates—without burdensome fees, gimmicks or other hassles

item.title: China’s Burned-Out Young Are Finding Something Unexpected in Mao
item.description: Plus, EU plans action against Chinese imports, Nike’s turnaround effort in China and a U.S. effort to loosen Beijing’s grip on critical minerals

item.title: Yemen’s Houthi Rebels Strike Two Airports in Saudi Arabia
item.description: The attacks follow a new counteroffensive by Saudi-backed forces seeking to push the rebels back from the Red Sea coast.

item.title: Hackers Use Chinese AI Tool to Hit South Korean Banks, Exposing New Risk
item.description: The attacks were the latest to highlight the vulnerability of even hardened targets to hackers using freely available artificial-intelligence tools.

item.title: France Spent for Years. Now the Bill Is Coming Due.
item.description: Plus, see how a reply-all email after Oct. 7 tore a business apart, and what Oura’s stalled IPO reveals about one-hit wonders.

item.title: Exporters to Get Extra Year for EU’s Methane Emission Rules, Von Der Leyen Says
item.description: Policymakers are racing to shield industry from the high cost of fuel triggered by conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine.

item.title: German Factory Orders Tumbled in August
item.description: Manufacturing orders in the eurozone’s largest economy fell 10.6% on month, as the conflict in the Middle East kept energy costs elevated.

item.title: How the Bolsonaro Family Made a Warp Speed Political Comeback in Brazil
item.description: The conservative movement is becoming the dominant force in Brazilian politics after Sunday’s national election.

item.title: France’s Appetite for ‘Magic Money’ Has Turned Into a Debt Bomb
item.description: After years of overspending, the country has emerged as one of Europe’s weakest links. Investors are bracing for things to get worse.

item.title: The Reply-All Email After Oct. 7 That Tore a Business Apart
item.description: The Israel-Gaza conflict remains a third rail in workplaces and beyond. At a Dallas therapy practice, it divided in-laws and escalated into firings and lawsuits.

item.title: Saudi-Backed Forces Launch Fight to Free Bab al-Mandeb From Houthis
item.description: The operation aims to take back the strategic Red Sea port of Mokha, which Iran-backed rebels have used to disrupt tanker traffic.

item.title: Threat of Iranian Drone Attack Prompted U.S. to Pull Bombers From U.K. Base
item.description: The planned attack was part of a broader Iranian plot to target the aircraft and kill American pilots at RAF Fairford, officials said.

item.title: Germany and France Are Proposing a New Weapon to Counter Flood of Chinese Goods
item.description: The countries, ahead of an EU leaders’ summit next week, are recommending lowering the bar for blocking Chinese products.

item.title: In China, Battle Is Raging for the Soul of Tibet
item.description: On the edge of the Himalayas, a tourist boomtown sells Chinese visitors a commoditized, politically palatable version of Tibetan culture.

item.title: Russia Probes Death of Woman Who Worked at Antiplague Institute
item.description: The Kremlin has sought to play down the death of the worker who contracted ”pneumonia of an unknown cause.”

item.title: FBI Arrests Alleged Chinese Agent Accused of Spying on Son of Taiwan Leader
item.description: The alleged foreign agent was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport before she could board a flight to Shanghai.
